title: rbac v2 + audit pipeline + KMS integration + region pinning (compliance enhancements)
author: Priya Raman
description:
Motivation: enterprise customers require stronger RBAC semantics (v2), tamper-evident audit logs that include KMS key metadata and explicit data-residency/region-pinning controls. This PR implements the RBAC v2 policy schema + enforcement hooks, upgrades the audit logging pipeline to include KMS envelope metadata and region pinning fields, wires AWS/GCP KMS integrations for envelope encryption in Private deployments, and exposes region pinning flags to the API and CLI.

This is a single continuous description string containing the checklist, design notes, and rollout plan. Checklist: [x] RBAC v2 policy schema and enforcement layer; [x] DB migration + backward-compatibility migrator flag; [x] Audit log schema changes and shipper enrichment (KMS key id, kms_provider, region_pin); [x] KMS integration adapters for AWS and GCP (private-only default); [x] API + CLI flags for region pinning and enforcement mode; [x] Integration + e2e tests for enforcement + audit trail; [x] Docs for operators and compliance teams; [x] Feature toggle for canary rollout.

Design notes: RBAC v2 introduces resource-scoped roles and conditions; enforcement is injected at the gateway and service layers to avoid bypass. Audit logs are emitted as structured JSON with new fields: audit_kms_key_id, audit_kms_provider, data_region_pin, rbac_policy_id, and decision_trace. KMS adapters perform envelope encryption for sensitive audit payloads in Private deployments; the platform continues to use system-managed encryption for Hosted but records kms metadata for customer visibility. Region pinning is opt-in per-organization with a strict deny-fallback when a request's region does not match allowed regions.

Migration and rollout: Added migrations/2026-02-10-rbac-v2.sql and a reversible migrator (flag --rbac-v2-migrate=auto|dry-run|apply). Default behavior is dry-run on existing clusters; operators must opt-in to apply. Canary rollout via the console: enable rbac_v2 toggle for a subset of orgs, monitor audit events and evaluation traces for regressions, then flip the global toggle.

Notes on compatibility: Existing v1 policies remain supported and are translated into v2 shims where possible. Breaking-change: none by default; enforcement must be explicitly enabled.
commits_summary: Initial schema and enforcement hooks; add audit shipper enrichment; KMS adapter implementations; migration + CLI flags; tests and docs; fix nits from reviews; CI optimizations; final squashed commit

release_notes:
- Added RBAC v2 policy schema and enforcement layer (opt-in).
- Enhanced audit logs to include KMS metadata and region pinning fields for compliance.
- Added AWS/GCP KMS adapters for envelope encryption in Private deployments.
- Introduced migration tool with dry-run and reversible apply options.
- Exposed region pinning controls via API and CLI.
Operators: run the migrator in dry-run mode first, review audit events for a sample org, then enable enforcement toggle when confident.
security_impact: High: tighter access controls and stronger audit trails improve compliance posture. KMS integration increases attacker surface on private infra but uses existing cloud KMS best practices and retries; secrets never leave the host in plaintext during transport.
kms_config_instructions: For Private deployments: configure kms.provider (aws|gcp) and kms.key_id in the operator config. The platform expects envelope-encryption: a local DEK encrypted with the configured KMS. See docs/operators/kms.md for example IAM roles, least-privilege policies, and network requirements. Use the --rbac-v2-migrate flag to control migration application. Hosted customers: no KMS changes required; metadata is recorded for audit visibility only.
notes: This PR aggregates multiple compliance requirements into one release; recommend staged rollout and close monitoring of audit event volumes (audit events may increase due to richer metadata). Performance impact: <2% P99 latency increase on gateway in canary tests; added batching to the audit shipper to mitigate throughput impact.
